B3 exports an internal, full trust artifact. No redaction, masking or field stripping. Public-safe and redacted receipt formats are V5-C4 work (issue #276), because canonical receipt content including metadata participates in the hash semantics verifyExportedBundle checks.
verifyExportedBundle must run before any response body is written; a failed verification returns no bundle under any status code.
Exceeding either ceiling returns 413 with no partial, truncated or paginated bundle; byte accounting uses actual serialized UTF-8 bytes rather than an estimate from receipt count.
An authenticated caller with zero receipts receives 200 with an empty verified bundle rather than 404, because absence of receipts is a truthful state.
The route must be declared in lib/http/route-auth-policy.js so an undeclared path stays 404 instead of leaking its existence through 401.

Named B3 falsification target: collectMaterializedReceiptEntries (lib/receipt/receipt-read-index.js:80) calls getAuditEvents with no limit and clones every matching receipt, and the chain is fully built before serialization, so actual serialized bytes are only measurable after the whole set is materialized. If both ceilings cannot be enforced within the authorized files without that unbounded materialization, the correct outcome is V4_B3_RECEIPT_EXPORT_USER_FLOW_BLOCKED_GAP.

Widening scope into lib/receipt/*, adding a limit parameter to the shared read index, approximating the byte ceiling from receipt count, or enforcing the ceiling only after materialization while calling it bounded are all explicitly incorrect resolutions.
